$comment: F.177 — THE SINGLE HOME FOR SUITE COUNT FLOORS. Read by `pnpm check:floors`
(scripts/check-suite-floors.mjs), which runs as the last step of `pnpm test`.
WHAT A FLOOR IS: the minimum number of tests a suite must COLLECT. The gate
fails only when a suite collects FEWER. Adding tests never breaks it.
WHY IT EXISTS: vitest exits 0 on a suite that collects fewer tests than it did
yesterday, because nothing tells it how many to expect. F.173's branch was cut
from the wrong parent and `pnpm test:scripts` reported 97 passed where it had
reported 106 — ZERO FAILURES, nine tests simply absent. It was caught by a
human remembering a number (DEV.156). This file is the detector that was
missing.
THESE NUMBERS ARE MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED. Every floor below is the count this
suite actually reported on 2026-10-03, read from its own JSON report. They are
set AT the measured count rather than below it: slack would be a hole the size
of the slack.
RAISING A FLOOR is optional housekeeping — the gate does not ask for it, and a
stale-low floor still catches a large drop.
LOWERING A FLOOR is a deliberate act. Do it in the SAME COMMIT as the test
deletion that justifies it, and say why in the message. **Never lower a floor
to get a build green** — that is the one move this file exists to make visible
(CLAUDE.md §11.1 ruling 1).
THE KNOWN WEAKNESS, stated rather than discovered: these are hand-maintained
literals the compiler cannot keep in step with anything — the F.167 shape. The
mitigation is that there is exactly ONE home, and that the gate's failure
message says what to do rather than only that a number is wrong.
`report` paths are relative to the repo root. NOTE that the scripts suite's
report lands in `scripts/` rather than the root, because vitest resolves
`--outputFile` against its config's directory and that suite runs with
`--config scripts/vitest.config.ts`. Measured, not assumed.

RAISED 2026-10-03: packages/db 224 -> 233, deliberately, to protect F.148’s nine agent_tokens tests. Raising is optional housekeeping and the gate did not ask for it; it is done here because those nine include the only assertion in the repository that an audit trigger EXISTS on a given table (F.168), and a floor that still read 224 would let all nine disappear without a word.
